notes: Hand-assembled, not `tubuild.py create` output: three of the legacy files wrap their whole body in `extern "C" { ... }`, which that generator's splitter refuses. The manifest entry is still tubuild's own (tubuild.build_manifest_entry).

Supersedes the coined-name entry ov002/Enemy, which carried the same .text span at status text-verified with 30 of the 31 members. The two additions are ordinal 4, _ZN12dEnemyBase_c14UpdateYoshiEatER10dBgCh_Actr, whose matching source landed under src/ after that entry was written, and ordinal 1, which is now spelled as the dEnemyBase_c::KillByInvincibleChar method its own shard recovered rather than the placeholder func_ov002_020ada40.

Genuine lifecycle source form: dEnemyBase_c declares ~dEnemyBase_c as its first non-inline virtual and this TU defines it, so this TU owns the class's key function and the compiler emits the whole chain's vtable and typeinfo as vague-linkage passengers. One `~dEnemyBase_c()` definition emits D2, D0 and D1 -- ordinals 27, 28 and 29 -- in the cartridge's own order.

_ZN12dEnemyBase_cC2Ev (ordinal 30) is written as a real constructor body, which is the form its legacy shard recovered and byte-matched. dEnemyBase_c.h DECLARES dEnemyBase_c() without defining it, so the base construction stays an out-of-line `bl` instead of being synthesised and inlined into the subclasses. One definition emits C1 and C2; the ROM keeps only C2, and the C1 this TU emits is licensed below as compiler-only output.

Members are spelled over the real classes wherever the cartridge bytes allow it, and each claim below was measured, not assumed: ordinal 6 (_ZN12dEnemyBase_c15IsGoingOffCliffER10dBgCh_Actrisbbi) is a real dEnemyBase_c::IsGoingOffCliff method taking its two by-value Fix12i parameters as themselves over real dBgCh_Lin/dBgPi locals; ordinals 2 and 4 use types.h's Vector3 rather than a POD shadow of it; and ordinal 26 uses the real 0x14-byte SurfaceInfo from include/SurfaceInfo.h. All 31 functions still reproduce byte-for-byte with objisolate and reloc-destination checks clean.

The file-scope PMF tables data_ov002_0210db80 and data_ov002_0210dbc0 are defined in this TU as non-const arrays, so mwcc emits __sinit_dEnemyBase_c.cpp, the ctor word, and the sixteen anonymous pointer-to-member descriptors. The thirteen PMF targets became real member definitions: eight on the TU-local dispatch receiver struct Aea30C (the type the first table's PMF representation was already formed on, kept so the (c->*pmf) call codegen is unchanged) and five on dEnemyBase_c for the UpdateDeath table. The handwritten src/__sinit_ov002_02100938.c is retired.

compiler_only_output.reason: Ordinal 30 is written as the real constructor `dEnemyBase_c::dEnemyBase_c()`, the form the legacy shard src/_ZN12dEnemyBase_cC2Ev.cpp recovered and byte-matched, and one such definition emits the complete-object C1 beside the licensed base-object C2. The ROM has no configured C1 home -- nothing constructs a standalone dEnemyBase_c, so the linker never kept one -- and no surviving function in this TU references it, which is the same disposition arm9/ActorBase takes for _ZN7fBase_cC1Ev.

dEnemyBase_c's key function is its out-of-line destructor -- ~dEnemyBase_c is the first virtual the header declares -- and this TU defines it, so mwccarm emits the whole ancestor chain's vague-linkage RTTI here as passengers: dEnemyBase_c -> dActor_c -> dBase_c -> fBase_c. fBase_c is the chain root, so its __class_type_info is emitted with no base word. The cartridge's own copy is at arm9:0x02086d70; romdata_check compares this object's bytes and relocations against that home before text-only isolation discards the duplicate.

__si_class_type_info for the second link of the chain; its +8 word relocates to _ZTI7fBase_c. ROM home arm9:0x02086e78.
Type-name string `7dBase_c\0`. ROM home arm9:0x02086e54, 0x9 bytes.
__si_class_type_info whose +8 word reaches _ZTI7dBase_c. ROM home arm9:0x0208e390. dActor_c is this class's direct base, so its record is inherited rather than owned here.
Type-name string `8dActor_c\0`. ROM home arm9:0x0208e384, 0xa bytes.

This class's OWN __si_class_type_info, +8 word relocating to _ZTI8dActor_c. ROM home ov002:0x021081c0, i.e. in this TU's own overlay -- this TU is the natural emitter, not a duplicating consumer, which is what ov002/da1up_c's matching row already records from the other side. The promotion route is text-only, so the manifest still claims no .data range and romdata_check proves the record and its relocations at that home before isolation discards this copy.

This class's own type-name string, ROM home ov002:0x021081cc, 0xf bytes -- the cartridge's spelling of the class, and the reason this TU, its header and its mangled members are named dEnemyBase_c rather than the project's former coined `Enemy`.

The vtable this TU is the key function for. ROM home ov002:0x021081e4, and verify's EXTRA line independently reports size=0x84 -- 33 words, the two-word RTTI prologue plus 31 dispatch slots. Ordinal 30 (_ZN12dEnemyBase_cC2Ev) stores the vptr through the ROM home's address, spelled data_ov002_021081e4, rather than through this locally emitted copy, so the store's addend stays 0 and no address-point bias applies on this route.

This TU odr-uses Vector3 by value (SpawnCoin builds a Vector3 temporary for dActor_c::Spawn's const-reference parameter), so mwccarm re-emits Vector3's trivial vague-linkage D1 alongside the licensed text. The cartridge keeps one copy at arm9:0x020072c0, kind:function(arm,size=0x4), and an enrolled source already owns it; rombuild compares this object's body against those cartridge bytes and refuses anything but byte-identical vague-linkage output before discarding the duplicate.
